IA.dc.html.title: Consolidation map · v3 shell → elizaOS phone

a1.text:
A · Grid + assistant pill (today's v3 shell)

FOR: familiar Android muscle memory; every surface one tap away; easy for third-party apps.

AGAINST: ~50 view tiles across launcher pages plus pager edge buttons, a tray, a command palette and widgets = several ways to navigate that compete. The agent reads as a bolt-on. Glance value is low; the grid shows what you own, not what matters now.

a2.text:
B · Chat is home

FOR: purest agentic story; one input for everything; tiny surface area to build.

AGAINST: blank-page problem (what can I ask?); zero glanceability (time, next event, unread need a question); history clutter becomes your home screen; direct manipulation tasks (scrub a calendar, swipe an inbox) get slower through words; private content sits on the default screen.

a3.text:
C · Ambient home + summonable chat (chosen)

FOR: glanceable (3 'Now' cards written by the agent, above every app in one grid); the composer sits where Android users expect search; one chat surface scales from pill to full over any view, so context is never lost; keeps AOSP gesture nav.

RISK: two ways to do things. Fix: every view action is also a chat command, and the pill is always one tap away.

n_modes.text:
Chat has one surface with four heights, not four features:

PILL (views): orb + type + talk. Minimum footprint, always reachable.
INPUT (home): a composer where Android puts search. Fastest path to a single command.
OVERLAY (half): answers land over the view you are in, so context stays visible and you can act on both.
FULL: history and long work. Same thread, same composer.

Voice isn't a fifth mode. It replaces the composer in whatever height you're in.

n_proto.text:
Press Play. Starts at power-on.

Home: swipe up from the bottom bar (or tap it), from anywhere. Back: swipe in from either edge. Notifications: pull down from the top. Chat: swipe up on Home, or the α pill in any app.

The rail on the right jumps to every app and its key screens, switches chat modes, and toggles light or dark.

Live site: alpha-phone-prototype.pages.dev
